A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ∇-GFlowNet study. Their complete main texts, equations, table, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original Stable Diffusion finetuning experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations and generated samples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments, including Table 1 and the quantitative and qualitative results throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: The main residual ∇-DB procedure and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v6 adds optional extensions: losses incorporating a learnable backward policy in Appendix C and an ODE-to-SDE conversion for applying the method to flow-matching models in Appendix G. These extend the procedure without replacing the evaluated algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image finetuning with Aesthetic Score, HPSv2 and ImageReward, retaining the same animal prompts and HPDv2 prompt coverage. The new flow-matching discussion provides no additional evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged. However, v6 corrects the reported residual-DB baseline loss in Equation 20 by adding the current-state predicted-reward and flow terms, and revises ReFL's gradient-path description. These are changes to comparator specifications; the PDFs do not establish that the comparisons were rerun.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes ReFL's stated gradient truncation from detaching x_t to forming x_t by denoising detached x_(t−1), thereby describing an additional differentiable transition. This is a reported training-procedure revision, without evidence of reruns. Model size, samplers, training budgets, prompt coverage, metrics and checkpoint-selection rules otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reward-temperature, subsampling, reward-attenuation, alternative-sampler, prior-strength and second-order-gradient analyses are retained with unchanged evidence. The wall-time comparisons and qualitative diversity examples are also unchanged despite appendix renumbering.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and report the same means, standard deviations and uncertainty bands. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical entries and the results displayed in Figures 2–31 are unchanged, including appendix curves and sample images. For example, the w_B=1 method retains an Aesthetic Score reward of 7.90 ± 0.09 and FID of 317 ± 15. No new empirical findings accompany the theoretical extensions.

T1.justification: v6 substantially expands the formal treatment while retaining Propositions 1 and 4 and their proofs. It adds learnable-backward-policy conditions, restates fixed-policy GFlowNet/soft-RL equivalence as Theorem 7, derives ∇-DB through soft Q-learning, expands the non-ideal-pretraining correction, and supplies the flow-matching SDE construction. Equation 20 also receives a mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly recast ∇-GFlowNet as a reinforcement-learning method and elevate its soft-RL connection into the contribution statement. The central novelty claim about using reward gradients in GFlowNets and the claims about convergence, diversity and prior preservation remain substantively intact.

C2.justification: v6 adds interpretations of backward-policy rewards as anchoring the optimum and benefiting optimization, and distinguishes fixed-backward-policy equivalence from jointly learned backward policies. Appendix G newly explains why deterministic flow matching requires stochastic conversion. The existing result interpretations and caveat about imperfect pretrained models are retained.

D1.justification: v3 introduces a learnable correction h for imperfect pretrained models without specifying its fitting objective. v6 Appendix E supplies a bidirectional training loss for h in Equation 61, making that proposal more explicit. Core experimental hyperparameters, hardware disclosure, Algorithm 1 and the project-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The brief soft-RL connection in v3 becomes a central positioning argument across v6's abstract, introduction, Section 2.2 and new Appendix D, including equivalence conditions and claimed distinctions. New citations include soft actor-critic, direct preference optimization, entropy-regularized-RL interpretations of GFlowNets and flow matching. Bibliographic consolidation and publication updates are separate presentational changes.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the abstract, introduction, Section 2.2 and baseline descriptions. New appendix sections are inserted, existing sections are relabeled, and references are standardized. Most method exposition, experimental discussion and the conclusion retain their earlier wording and organization.

P2.justification: Table 1 and all 31 figures retain their content and display designs. Layout changes include moving the final contribution bullet onto page 1, shifting Figure 1 upward, shortening reference entries and reflowing early appendix material. No evidence panels are added, removed or redrawn.

improvement.justification: v6 restores missing terms in the baseline loss and makes the soft-RL relationship, applicability boundaries and correction-learning objective more explicit, providing a modest gain in clarity and reproducibility. The empirical evidence is unchanged. The added theory also introduces a temperature-scaling inconsistency: Equation 57 omits the beta factor implied by its stated soft-value definition. This limits the benefit of the expanded formal discussion.
